notes.132v.12: carnanx odia ... samsodina are kept as words of power. '..u. ach', 'ir', '..tw' and '.u.' are unexplained, perhaps abbreviations or damage; left as they stand. gast ('guest, stranger') seems to address the worm. eiter may be 'pus' rather than 'poison'.

nodes.text: and of all the kinds of worms that are feeding
May the worm be dead now, today and
forevermore. In the name of the Lord. Amen. The Our Father. This you must
say three times. Against the poison
you must say it: carnanx odia, carnanx
edia, inmensina, samsodina. Guest, are you *ir*
N.? ..tw are you .u.? May they melt away
now, in the name of the Holy Spirit.
